meta.note: Hand-authored seed for build and demo only. Every row is synthetic. EXCLUDE from all real research aggregates and from the public corpus once real data flows. Purge or hard-fence before public launch. Proportions are hand-set, not produced by the slicer, so the demo is deterministic. Fictional songs and usernames; diverse fake-listener voices, not the house voice. Starter set; expand toward the 100-150 target later.

resonances.story: I was 19 and ready to disappear. This song did not glorify any of that. It found me at the bottom and somehow made the bottom feel survivable, like someone had been there and left a light on. I came out of that winter because of it.
Everyone calls it filth. Maybe. But the one honest line in it cracked something open in me that years of nicer songs never touched. I started telling the truth after that.
It put words to a rage I had been swallowing. Not to feed it. To finally look at it. That was the day I stopped pretending I was fine.
Honestly it just matched my mood the week my dad left. The song was there. I do not think the song did much. I was a wreck and it was loud.
Felt like a hit of something. Big, then nothing. I mistook the size of it for meaning for a long time.
It found me at the exact wrong-right moment and told me I was not the only one down there. I kept going. That is not nothing.
I have played this at every low point for six years. It does not lift me up so much as sit with me. But sitting with me kept me alive twice.
People are going to hate that I say this saved me. It is an ugly song. It told me the ugly truth I needed and I am still here.
It felt like church for a second. Then I realized it was just dressing up my resentment as righteousness. Took me a while to see the costume.
Pumped me up to do nothing but stew. Felt profound at 2am. Felt empty by noon.
I thought it understood me. It only flattered the worst version of me.
Some nights it is a real comfort, some nights it is just noise that was on. Hard to say what it actually did.
Decent enough. Reminded me of a person more than it moved me.
This was playing the summer everything changed. The song is fine. The summer is what I am really remembering.
My sister and I drove to this on repeat. I cannot hear it without the car, the heat, her laugh. That is hers, not the song.
Bookmark for a year I will never get back. The music is almost incidental.
A little lift, a little nostalgia, a little of something I cannot name. All three at once.
Genuinely steadied me on a bad commute. Modest but real.
It gave me a way to think about leaving that did not feel like running. I made a real decision because of it.
Lovely, and tangled up with my first apartment. Half the warmth is the apartment.
Closest thing to prayer I have without a religion. It lifts me every single time, on its own merit, no story attached.
It genuinely makes me more patient with people for about a day. I can feel it working.
Everyone swears by this one. For me it is just the song from my wedding. Beautiful, but it is the day I feel, not the song.
One play and I called my brother for the first time in two years. Whatever that is, it was the song.
I know what this song is. I am not proud of loving it. But it pulled me up out of a night I might not have walked away from. I cannot explain it.
It does the thing the good ones do. Quiet, clean, lifts you without asking anything back.
Real lift, but I will admit some of it is the friend who showed it to me.
You read this as me wallowing. It was the opposite. It was the first time I let myself be angry on purpose and it broke a logjam.
After review the read changed: this is genuine release, not stewing. Worth the contest.
Small daily lift. Nothing dramatic. Keeps me even.
Mostly it reminds me of a kitchen and a person. Pleasant. Not the song.
Everyone treats this like a masterpiece. To me it is just my grandmother's kitchen. I love it for her, not for it.
Beautiful song, sure. But what I feel is the road trip, not the music.
It is the first dance at our wedding. I cannot judge the song. It is just us, now.
